title: Resolution of vectors; unit vectors
notes:
## 1. Topic Introduction — Splitting a Vector into Useful Pieces

Resolution is the reverse of addition: one vector becomes two (or three) components whose sum is the original. Choosing the right axes turns awkward angled problems into independent one-dimensional ones — the technique behind every projectile, inclined-plane and work calculation.

## 2. Fundamental Concepts

### 2.1 Rectangular components

A vector $\vec A$ making angle θ with the x-axis resolves into:
- **x-component:** $A_x = A\cos\theta$
- **y-component:** $A_y = A\sin\theta$
- Magnitude recombines: $A = \sqrt{A_x^2 + A_y^2}$
- Direction: $\tan\theta = A_y/A_x$

**NEB 2024 (3m):** $\vec A$ has magnitude 50 m at 37° with the +x axis:
$A_x = 50\cos37° = 50 \times 0.8 = 40$ m; $A_y = 50\sin37° = 50 \times 0.6 = 30$ m.
**Rectangular components: 40 m along x and 30 m along y** (check: √(40² + 30²) = 50 ✓).

### 2.2 Unit vectors

$\hat i, \hat j, \hat k$ are unit vectors along x, y, z (magnitude 1, dimensionless direction markers). Any vector:
$$\vec A = A_x\hat i + A_y\hat j + A_z\hat k, \qquad A = \sqrt{A_x^2 + A_y^2 + A_z^2}$$
A unit vector along any vector: $\hat A = \vec A/A$.

### 2.3 Addition by components (NEB 2021)

$\vec R = (A_x + B_x)\hat i + (A_y + B_y)\hat j$ — components add, then recombine:
$R = \sqrt{R_x^2 + R_y^2}$, $\tan\alpha = R_y/R_x$.

Example (2021): $(3\hat i + 4\hat j) + (5\hat i - 12\hat j) = 8\hat i - 8\hat j$ m; $R = 8\sqrt2 ≈ 11.3$ m at 45° below +x.

### 2.4 Oblique components

A vector can also be resolved along two non-perpendicular directions (e.g. parallel and perpendicular to an inclined plane) — the components then satisfy the parallelogram law in reverse. Perpendicular (rectangular) components are used because they are independent: changing one never changes the other.

## 3. Why Resolution Works — The Independence of Components

Horizontal and vertical motions (or forces) do not interfere: the x-physics and y-physics can be solved separately and recombined. This independence is why:
- Projectile motion splits into uniform horizontal motion + accelerated vertical motion.
- A block on an incline uses $mg\sin\theta$ (along plane) and $mg\cos\theta$ (into plane).
- Work is $F s\cos\theta$ — only the component of force along displacement works.

## 4. Conceptual Relationships

- **To Topic 3:** resolution and the parallelogram law are inverse operations — the components are the sides, the vector is the diagonal.
- **To Topic 5:** the dot product extracts components ($A_x = \vec A\cdot\hat i$); the cross product builds perpendicular vectors.
- **To Kinematics:** projectile analysis is resolution in action.
- **To Dynamics:** inclined planes, banking and equilibrium all resolve forces.

## 5. Exam Orientation and Previous Year Questions (NEB)

### 5.1 Verified PYQs from the solved-paper bank

| Year | Unit | Topic | Question | Marks | Type |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2080/2024 | Vectors | Resolution | A vector A has magnitude 50 m and makes an angle of 37° with the positive x-axis. Find its rectangular components. | 3 | Numerical |
| 2077/2021 | Vectors | Addition by components | Add the vectors (3î + 4ĵ) m and (5î − 12ĵ) m and express the resultant in magnitude and direction form. | 3 | Numerical |

### 5.2 Model answers

**Q1 (3m, 2024):** $A_x = A\cos\theta = 50\cos37° = 40$ m; $A_y = A\sin\theta = 50\sin37° = 30$ m. The rectangular components are **40 m (x) and 30 m (y)**; verification: $\sqrt{40^2 + 30^2} = 50$ m.

**Q2 (3m, 2021):** $\vec R = (3+5)\hat i + (4-12)\hat j = 8\hat i - 8\hat j$ m; $R = \sqrt{64+64} = 8\sqrt2 ≈ 11.3$ m; $\tan\alpha = -1 → \alpha = 45°$ below the +x axis.

### 5.3 Common examination mistakes

1. Swapping sin and cos — the component **adjacent** to θ takes cos; the component opposite takes sin.
2. Using degrees where radians are needed (or vice versa) in calculator mode errors.
3. Forgetting to state the direction of the resultant after finding its magnitude.
4. Treating unit vectors as having units — $\hat i$ is dimensionless; the units ride on the components.
5. Adding magnitudes instead of components when vectors point in different directions.

The y-component of the same vector is:

mcqs.explanation: A unit vector carries only direction — magnitude 1, no units.

If Aₓ = 6 N and A_y = 8 N, the magnitude of A⃗ is:
Perpendicular components are preferred because they:
options: Are independent — changing one does not affect the other
mcqs.explanation: Independence of perpendicular directions lets each axis be solved separately.

mcqs.question: A force of 20 N at 60° above the horizontal has vertical component:
The direction of R⃗ = 8î − 8ĵ is:
mcqs.explanation: tan α = −8/8 = −1 → 45° below the +x axis (fourth quadrant).

summary: Resolution splits one vector into components that add back to it. Rectangular components of a vector at angle θ are $A_x = A\cos\theta$ and $A_y = A\sin\theta$, recombining as $A = \sqrt{A_x^2 + A_y^2}$ with $\tan\theta = A_y/A_x$ — so 50 m at 37° becomes 40 m and 30 m (NEB 2024). Unit vectors $\hat i, \hat j, \hat k$ carry pure direction, letting any vector be written $A_x\hat i + A_y\hat j + A_z\hat k$; addition then proceeds component by component: $(3\hat i + 4\hat j) + (5\hat i - 12\hat j) = 8\hat i - 8\hat j$ m, magnitude $8\sqrt2$ m at 45° below the x-axis (NEB 2021). Perpendicular components are independent — the fact that makes projectiles, inclines and work calculations solvable one axis at a time.
